- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecasted drop幅度 by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward; cap forecast decline to 1–2% below peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 2–5% upward bias in 3–7 day horizon.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overestimate volatility; smooth forecast curve by reducing standard deviation by 15–20%.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates downward trend after recent lows; adjust by adding 3–5% upward bias if sentiment is weakly positive.
- If sentiment is positive and price is near recent high, model often overestimates peak; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and shift peak 1–2 days later.
